dossier_meta.catalog_title: Open problem: tighter bounds for linear graph-codes
dossier_meta.statement_text: Establish tighter bounds for the maximum possible cardinality of a linear family of graphs on $[n]$ in which no symmetric difference is a copy of a fixed graph $H$ with an even number of edges.
dossier_meta.context_text: The paper notes that for any fixed graph $H$ with an even number of edges the maximum size of a linear $H$-code is $o\bigl(2^{\binom{n}{2}}\bigr)$, but the proof via Ramsey's Theorem yields very weak quantitative bounds. Theorem 1.6 gives a tight result for the family $\mathcal{K}$ of all cliques as a model for what such tight results could look like.
